J1 USB-C receptacle, 16-pin power+USB2 type (no SuperSpeed pads) per blocks.md B1. NON-NEGOTIABLE CRITERIA VERIFIED AGAINST THE PRIMARY DATASHEET (GCT drawing USB4105, rev B3, fetched and read directly, not from JLC's attribute field alone): Electrical table states 'Current Rating: 5.00A collectively for VBUS pins, 6.25A collectively for GND pins' (exact match to the 5.00A-collective wording blocks.md demands) and 'Voltage Rating: 48V DC'. Pin table confirms the full 16-pin map (A1/A12/B1/B12=GND, A4/A9/B4/B9=VBUS, A5=CC1, B5=CC2, A6/A7/B6/B7=Dp/Dn, A8/B8=SBU1/SBU2) - matches blocks.md's wiring facts (CC1=A5, CC2=B5, DP/DM shorted at the chip) exactly. CORRECTION TO ARCHITECTURE (worth flagging - a good-news deviation, not a compromise): blocks.md B1 states 'the GCT USB4105 class is rated 20V DC, which is our maximum with zero margin' - the live datasheet for the actual orderable part (this exact LCSC SKU, USB4105-GF-A-120) reads 48V DC, not 20V. Either blocks.md's research pulled a different/older GCT part or misread the source; this verification supersedes it with a directly-read primary datasheet. Real margin: 48V vs the >=24V floor, 2x better than even the 'USB4085 class is 48V' fallback blocks.md described as the safer option. COST NOTE: this drives J1 to ~$0.92-1.14/unit, well above decisions.md D14's rough $0.15-0.35 estimate (which assumed a generic 20V-class SHOU HAN/Korean-Hroparts part at ~$0.07-0.18 - those DO exist with 16P+5A specs, e.g. TYPE-C-31-M-12 C165948 at $0.18, but are all rated exactly 20V, the zero-margin case blocks.md explicitly rejects). No alternate listed: every other 16-pin, >=5A-rated candidate found live is 20V-class (rejected per blocks.md's own criterion); the only other >=24V options are USB4105-GF-A (12-pin, drops 2 of the 4 VBUS/GND redundant contacts) or USB4085-GF-A (C7095263, THT/Plugin not SMD) - neither matches blocks.md's 16-pin SMD spec as well as this part.

parts.role: D1 unidirectional TVS at the connector, first element on VBUS, per blocks.md B1/D5 - NOT optional (cites a real CH224 trigger-board teardown destroyed at 20V from a cable inductive spike with no TVS fitted). HARD REQUIREMENT: my assignment flagged clamp voltage as the parameter that matters most here ('the CH224K dies above ~22-24V, so clamp matters more than the part family'), so this was verified against the primary datasheet, not just JLC's attribute field. The originally-named class (TDS2221PW / Semtech SI21-03, DFN 1.6x1.0mm, 28V clamp at 22A/8-20us) returned ZERO live results under either name search - not currently orderable via this catalog. SUBSTITUTED with TI's TVS2200 'Flat-Clamp' device instead of the more common PTVS22VS1UR-class (Nexperia's part, which is what most JLC listings under '22V TVS' actually are): fetched TI's real datasheet (SLVSED5A) and confirmed Vrwm=22V (exact match to blocks.md's '22V working'), max clamp 28.4V at 40A/8-20us (near-exact match to blocks.md's '~28V max clamp, 22A at 8/20us' - same test condition, TI's part handles even MORE current at a comparable clamp). TI's own Applications list names 'USB Type-C Vbus' explicitly, and its whole 'Flat-Clamp' technology exists specifically to clamp lower than a 'Traditional TVS' at the same standoff (shown in the datasheet's own comparison plot) - this is arguably a BETTER-engineered match to blocks.md's numeric target than a same-family PTVS22VS1UR part would be, whose headline 25.9-26.9V breakdown / 35.5V clamp (BORN/Nexperia-clone figures, confirmed via BORN's datasheet) sit closer to the class blocks.md explicitly rejected ('NOT a 24V SMAJ/SMBJ - that class clamps at 38-39V'). PACKAGE DEVIATION FROM blocks.md's ASSUMED CLASS: WSON-6 2x2mm (6 pads, all IN/GND commoned - electrically a plain 2-terminal device) vs the assumed DFN 1.6x1.0mm 2-pin footprint; still small, fits blocks.md D8's 'hugging the main run' placement note without issue, but flag for the P4/P6 footprint pull since it needs a different library footprint than a generic 2-pin TVS diode.

parts.role: F1, the aux-tap resettable PPTC (decisions.md D0.1/D1 - the sole resettable element on the whole board, deliberately NOT in the 5A main path; see D1's full reasoning for why a main-path PPTC was rejected). EXACT match to the part class blocks.md B6 names by MPN ('BSMD1206-100-30V class, ~$0.10') - confirmed to the cent live. CAUTION FOR OTHER SEARCHERS: JLC's catalog also carries a visually-similar '...-050-30V' / 'JK-nSMD050-30' family in the same 1206/1812 packages at similar price/stock, but those are 500mA hold / 1A trip - HALF this board's required 1A hold current. Verified the '100' in this part number (and the 'Hold Current: 1A' attribute) before selecting, not just the package/voltage match.

C1, connector-side VBUS bulk cap (blocks.md B1/D5, must total ~22uF, 50V-rated not 25V - X5R loses most of its marked capacitance under 20V DC bias on a 25V-rated part, per V7). SOURCING DEVIATION: searched extensively for a single 22uF/50V/1210 X5R MLCC (blocks.md's primary spec) - every live hit at 50V-and-up in a 1210 case came back either an ELECTROLYTIC/polymer can (wrong technology - blocks.md wants ceramic; ripple-current/ESR/ESL characteristics are wrong for this role) or, among true 1210 ceramics, every 22uF part found is rated 16V or 25V (all show up cheap and Basic-adjacent, but the wrong voltage class - would derate WORSE than the already-marginal 25V case V7 warns against). No 22uF/50V/1210 ceramic SKU with real stock turned up under several query variants. USED THE FALLBACK blocks.md ITSELF PRE-AUTHORIZED for exactly this situation (B1/summary table: 'C1 | 22uF/50V X5R 1210 | Basic | or 2x 10uF/50V 1206'): 2x this part in parallel = 20uF at 50V, same total ballpark as the 22uF target (charging-current math in blocks.md B1 used 22uF only as a round number against the 100uF cSnkBulkPd ceiling; 20uF is materially the same headroom). This exact part is Basic tier (unlike every real 22uF/1210 candidate, which are all Extended) and by far the best-stocked 50V/10uF/1206 option (3.1M vs the next-closest non-Basic listing's ~500k). COST NOTE: at 2x $0.3735, this line costs ~$0.75/board - well above decisions.md D14's rough '13R + 5C (incl. 22uF/50V 1210): $0.15' estimate for ALL passives combined; a 50V-rated ceramic bulk cap at this capacitance is inherently one of the pricier passives on the board, not a sourcing shortfall. P4/P6 NOTE: architecture's schematic (sheets.md) names one ref 'C1' for this role; realizing it as 2 parallel physical parts needs a second reference designator at schematic-generation time (e.g. C1 + a paired C1B/C16) - flagging so P4 doesn't silently drop one.

C2, connector-side VBUS bulk companion (blocks.md B1, decisions.md D5). C3 (the LDO input decoupler this part used to also serve) is removed at amendment A1 with the LDO itself - this line now covers C2 only. Sits on VBUS so needs >=25V rating per the assignment's blanket VBUS-cap rule; 50V clears it with margin. Same exact MPN/LCSC already used and DRC-verified across this pipeline's other boards (usb-buck LEARNINGS precedent) - massive stock (105M), no sourcing risk at all.

C5, the datasheet-mandated cap on U1's VDD pin (decisions.md D2, B2) - VDD to GND, directly across the shunt regulator's output. C4 (the LDO output bulk cap this part used to also serve) is removed at amendment A1 with the LDO itself - this line now covers C5 only. Only needs >=16V (a 3.3V-class shunt node) but this 50V-rated Basic part is cheaper and better-stocked than the nearest 16V-rated Extended option found live, so it is used unchanged. Same exact MPN already used (and DRC-verified) in this pipeline's usb-buck board.

TWO distinct roles, same value/part, 0603 thick film: R1 (10k series into U1 pin 8 VBUS-sense, mandatory per D5) and R8 (10k collector pull-up for Q1B's inverter stage, D4). R3/R4/R5 moved to a dedicated 100k line at amendment A1 (decisions.md D3) - see that entry; they are no longer part of this combined line. NOTE min_qty 1317 is this listing's reel MOQ (same pattern already accepted in this pipeline's usb-buck board for the same UNI-ROYAL 10k part) - not a board-qty-10 issue, JLC's assembly service does not require buying a full reel for a 2-piece need.

R3/R4/R5, 100k pull-ups to /VDD for SW1's CFG1/2/3 (decisions.md D3, amended A1 - value raised from 10k to 100k and the rail changed from a since-removed +3V3 to /VDD). Pull-UP polarity is the safety-relevant choice: open contact, unpopulated switch, or broken contact all resolve to '1XX' = 5V, the lowest profile. Value is the single most consequential number the P3 datasheet extract changed: at the 5V profile the whole /VDD node is fed only 1.7mA through R2's dropper; three 10k pull-ups would draw 990uA (58% of that budget), three 100k pull-ups draw 99uA (6%) - this Basic-tier part is what makes the housekeeping budget close. Same UNI-ROYAL 0603 family as the rest of the board's resistors.

alternates.note: UNI-ROYAL, single-part 2512 1k 1W Extended alternate if the 2-series-1206 assembly is undesired: stock 179029, $0.0488@1. No Basic-tier 2512 1k exists live (checked directly with --basic-only: zero results in that package), which is why the series-1206 alternate ships instead, per the P3 assignment's decision rule.

parts.role: R2 dropper, VBUS -> U1 pin1 VDD (decisions.md D2/A1 - the datasheet's shunt-regulator dropper, NOT the pre-amendment LDO-isolation resistor). SHIPPED THE APPROVED ALTERNATE: 2x 510R 1206 in series (~1020R, within the 1k target) instead of a single 2512 1k part, because no Basic-tier 1k/2512 exists live (verified directly: a --basic-only search on '1k 2512' returns only 0402/0603/1206/0805 packages, zero 2512 hits) - the assignment's fallback condition is met. Extended-tier 1k/2512 parts DO exist (e.g. C31885 at $0.0488, recorded as an alternate above) but the series-1206 alternate was preferred per the assignment's explicit decision rule. Power check: 0.313W at 21V (worst case, decisions.md D2) split across 2 parts = 0.157W each against each part's 250mW rating = 63% (~1.6x derating) - matches decisions.md D2's own pre-approved figure for this exact fallback ('0.157 W each in 0.25 W parts') exactly; short of the 3x derating wanted for the single-2512 path, but the explicitly pre-approved number for this alternate. At the 5V profile floor the pair carries ~1.7mA (1.1mA at 4.4V low line, decisions.md D2), negligible dissipation. Placement note carried from decisions.md D8 A1: keep >=8mm from U1's baseplate (its only heat path) - applies to both series resistors.
R6, from VBUS through D2 (6.2V zener) into Q1A's base - sets the ~6.7V window-detector trip point (decisions.md D4). Delivers 243uA base drive at the 9V profile's 8.55V floor, 1.93mA/25mW at 20V.

R7, base-emitter shunt on Q1A (decisions.md D4) - sinks zener knee leakage (needs >149uA to reach 0.7V, versus a few uA of real leakage at 5.25V) so a soft knee cannot fake a high profile. NOTE min_qty 766 is this listing's reel MOQ, not a board-qty-10 issue.

R9, base resistor driving Q1B from Q1A's collector node /HV_OK, completing the inverter that lights exactly one of D5/D6 (decisions.md D4). NOTE min_qty 800 is this listing's reel MOQ, not a board-qty-10 issue.

R10, D3 'PWR' LED series resistor, now bus-referenced off /VIND (decisions.md D4/A1 - previously a shared 680R line feeding all four LEDs off a regulated +3V3 rail; that rail and the LDO behind it are gone). Power check (task-specified naive worst case, V^2/R at 21V): 441/3300 = 0.134W against this 1206's 250mW rating = 54%, ~1.9x derating. Realistic figure accounting for the LED's own Vf drop (decisions.md A1's own math): 0.11W, ~2.3x derating - matches decisions.md's stated figure exactly. D3 is always on (0.76mA at 4.4V to 5.8mA at 21V per D4), so this is the one LED resistor that genuinely sees the full bus range continuously. No Basic-tier 3.3k 1206 exists live (checked directly with --basic-only: the two hits returned are 0603/0805 packages, not 1206).

R12, D5 '5V ONLY' (red) LED series resistor, off /VIND (decisions.md D4/A1). Conducts ONLY below the ~6.7V window trip (bus 4.4-5.25V) since D5 is reverse/off above that - so despite the task's blanket 'check P=V^2/R at 21V' instruction, R12 never actually sees 21V across it with current flowing (D6 conducts instead at high bus, D5 sits open). Real worst case is at the top of D5's conduction window (~5.25V): P ~= 7mW per decisions.md A1's own math, against this 0603's 100mW rating - over 10x margin. A naive full-21V assumption would wrongly read as a 294%-of-rating violation; noted here so a future check does not misread it.

R13, D6 'PROFILE OK' (green) LED series resistor, off /VIND (decisions.md D4/A1). Conducts ONLY above the ~6.7V window trip (bus 8.55-21V). Power check (task-specified naive worst case, V^2/R at 21V): 441/4700 = 0.094W against this 0805's 125mW rating = 75%, ~1.33x derating. Realistic figure accounting for the LED's Vf drop (decisions.md A1's own math): 0.08W, ~1.56x derating - matches decisions.md's stated figure exactly. This is the tightest margin of the three LED resistors (R10/R12/R13) but still positive and it is the architecture's own settled value, not a P3 substitution.

R14, NEW at amendment A1 (decisions.md A1.2): the VBUS -> /VIND housekeeping link, a 0 ohm jumper, not present in the P2-pass BOM. Without it, all eight housekeeping taps (the LED row etc.) would hang directly off the 5A VBUS net and check_current would demand 1.75mm copper on every run out to them; behind this link, /VIND is declared width-only (pdn:false, 50mA) and routes at the fab floor. Carries the LED row's current (up to ~32mA max per decisions.md A1.2) - any resistance/current rating comfortably covers that; this 100mW/0Ohm Basic part is the standard JLC 0603 jumper, massive stock, trivial cost.
